context: Marimekko chart showing global market share across 5 industries (Electronics, Healthcare, Automotive, Energy, Finance) broken into 4 customer segments; column width encodes industry revenue in $B, row height encodes segment share within each industry.
first_impression: Structurally honest Marimekko — area correctly encodes two-dimensional proportional data via treemapSliceDice, with a clearly labeled subtitle and a correct 0–100% Y-axis.
what_works: Area encoding is mathematically correct: treemap.sum() uses data-derived values so column width ∝ industry revenue share and row height ∝ segment share within industry, giving area ∝ global segment revenue. Y-axis is fixed at 0–100%, which is appropriate and not misleading for a fully proportional chart.
what_doesnt: The hierarchy .sort() reorders subcategories by descending value within each industry column, so the same segment (e.g., 'Consumer') appears at different Y-positions across columns, breaking cross-column comparison — an interpretive honesty issue. Data joins use no key function (.data(leaves).join('rect') without d => d.id), which would corrupt transitions if data were updated, and white text on the #CCBB44 'Emerging' yellow-green cells has poor contrast.
